display_title: [jax-buildcop] Reuse compiled shapes in Bessel kn tests to avoid shard timeouts

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Reuse compiled shapes in Bessel kn tests to avoid shard timeouts

`_kn` in `jax._src.scipy.bessel` is a `@custom_jvp` function wrapping `@partial(jit, static_argnums=(0,))` (and for complex inputs compiles both `_kn_complex_first_quadrant` and `_iv_first_quadrant_complex`). Calling `_kn` or its JVP/grad on secondary test arrays (`special_xs`, `special_zs`, `overflow_zs`, and 0D scalars `0.0`, `tiny_x`, `z0`) with shapes different from the primary test array (`x` / `zs`), or wrapping `jax.grad` in `_CompileAndCheck`, triggers redundant XLA compilations for every `(n, dtype)` case.

Pad secondary test arrays to match `x.shape` / `zs.shape` and evaluate pole gradients at `zs.shape` in `test_kn_grad` so the cached 1D executables are reused, cutting `test_kn_grad*` shard execution times in half and `test_kn_orders_and_regimes*` by ~5x.

display_title: [ROCm] Compile IFRT IR MPMD programs on PJRT-backed IFRT clients

head_commit.message:
Compile IFRT IR MPMD programs on PJRT-backed IFRT clients

`compile_mpmd` compiled IFRT IR programs with the client's default
compiler. On PJRT-backed IFRT clients, such as the CPU client and PJRT
plugin clients, that is `PjRtCompiler`, which only accepts HLO
programs, so compiling any MPMD program failed with "PjRtCompiler
requires an HloProgram".

On those clients, compile with XLA's `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` instead.
It compiles each atom program through the client with
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler`, and the resulting executable runs the
program with the IFRT IR interpreter. Other clients still use their
default compiler.

`_sdy_mpmd` also imported `jax.jaxlib._jax`, which does not exist in
jaxlib wheels, so importing `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd` failed. It now imports
`jaxlib._jax`, as it already does for `jaxlib._hlo`.

The new `tests/sdy_mpmd_test.py` compiles and runs a program over two
single-device meshes on the CPU client. It is skipped before jaxlib
extension version 523, which this change introduces.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] Eliminate redundant XLA compilations in `hyp1f1`, `hyp2f1`, and `betaln` gradient tests

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Eliminate redundant XLA compilations in `hyp1f1`, `hyp2f1`, and `betaln` gradient tests

`hyp1f1` and `hyp2f1` previously applied `promote_args_inexact` inside `@custom_jvp` and `@jit`, wrapped `_hyp1f1_x_derivative` and `_hyp2f1_x_derivative` in an outer `@jit`, and passed the differentiated parameter array `p` directly to `_hyp1f1_param_derivative` / `_hyp2f1_param_derivative`. On mixed-shape or mixed-dtype inputs (such as in `testScipySpecialFun`), this forced `_hyp1f1_x_derivative` and `_hyp2f1_x_derivative` to re-inline and recompile the full `hyp1f1` / `hyp2f1` loop graphs instead of reusing the cached `@jit` executable, and caused `_hyp1f1_param_derivative` / `_hyp2f1_param_derivative` to miss the `@jit` cache across parameters of different broadcast shapes.

- Move `promote_args_inexact` into public `hyp1f1` and `hyp2f1` wrappers ahead of `@custom_jvp`, drop the outer `@jit` on `_hyp1f1_x_derivative` and `_hyp2f1_x_derivative` so `_hyp1f1(a + 1, b + 1, x)` and `_hyp2f1(a + 1, b + 1, c + 1, x)` hit the primal `@jit` cache, and select `p` via a scalar index inside `_hyp1f1_param_derivative` and `_hyp2f1_param_derivative` so all parameter derivatives share one compiled executable per input shape tuple.
- In `testBetalnGrads`, pad secondary extreme-input arrays to `a.shape` to reuse the compiled VJP and split `order=2` forward-mode checks into `testBetalnSecondOrderGrads` so first- and second-order AD compilations distribute across shards without reducing test coverage.

Allow mixed `Auto` meshes in `SearchSorted` and `jnp.histogram`.

allocations could not be expressed with WG semantics.

display_title: Allow mixed `Auto` meshes in `SearchSorted` and `jnp.histogram`.

head_commit.message:
Allow mixed `Auto` meshes in `SearchSorted` and `jnp.histogram`.

`SearchSorted` is a `HiPrimitive` that runs its own `_sharding_rule` instead of `lax_utils.call_sharding_rule`, and previously rejected any two non-empty input meshes that were unequal. When one operand is created under an all-`Auto` context `AbstractMesh` (such as `bin_edges` in `jnp.histogram` under `use_abstract_mesh`, with or without `out_sharding`) while the other carries a concrete all-`Auto` device mesh, `SearchSorted._sharding_rule` raised `ValueError: sharding meshes must match`. Match `call_sharding_rule` by resolving mismatched all-`Auto` operand meshes to the active context mesh when no `Explicit` axis is active.

In `jnp.histogram`, check `ats != wts` only when neither mesh is empty and either `a` or `weights` has an `Explicit` mesh axis (matching `core.cmp_shape_shd_mat_memsp`), so non-`Explicit` shardings on different `Auto` meshes are accepted while mixed `Explicit` and `Auto` meshes are still rejected.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [jax-buildcop] Reuse compiled shapes in Bessel kn tests to avoid shard timeouts

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Reuse compiled shapes in Bessel kn tests to avoid shard timeouts

`_kn` in `jax._src.scipy.bessel` is a `@custom_jvp` function wrapping `@partial(jit, static_argnums=(0,))` (and for complex inputs compiles both `_kn_complex_first_quadrant` and `_iv_first_quadrant_complex`). Calling `_kn` or its JVP/grad on secondary test arrays (`special_xs`, `special_zs`, `overflow_zs`, and 0D scalars `0.0`, `tiny_x`, `z0`) with shapes different from the primary test array (`x` / `zs`), or wrapping `jax.grad` in `_CompileAndCheck`, triggers redundant XLA compilations for every `(n, dtype)` case.

Pad secondary test arrays to match `x.shape` / `zs.shape` and evaluate pole gradients at `zs.shape` in `test_kn_grad` so the cached 1D executables are reused, cutting `test_kn_grad*` shard execution times in half and `test_kn_orders_and_regimes*` by ~5x.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Allow allocating up to 576 TMEM columns on sm_107f.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Allow allocating up to 576 TMEM columns on sm_107f.

On sm_107f, TMEM has 576 columns per CTA
instead of 512, but the columns past 512 can only be used through
`tcgen05.alloc.exclusive`, which must be the only TMEM allocation that exists
at any time and must be released with `tcgen05.dealloc.exclusive`.

TMEM allocations of more than 512 columns are now lowered to an exclusive
allocation of all 576 columns on sm_107f. Since nothing else can be allocated
alongside an exclusive allocation, and while context switching
no CTAs can use the remaining 576 - 512 columns, there is no benefit to allocating fewer columns.

The mode is selected automatically from the number of columns, so
there is no new user-facing API, and allocations of at most 512 columns are
unchanged. This means that now if someone wants to use this feature on
sm107f they have to allocate once and use slice_tmem API.

Other architectures keep the 512-column limit.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Improve tail precision and gradients of jax.scipy.stats.gumbel_r/gumbel_l

head_commit.message:
Improve tail precision of some jax.scipy.stats functions

gumbel_r.sf was computed as 1 - exp(-exp(-z)), which is 0 once exp(-exp(-z))
rounds to 1 (float32: x >= 20 for the standard distribution, float64: x >= 40),
where scipy returns 2e-9 and 4e-18. gumbel_l.logcdf used log(-expm1(-exp(z))),
which is 0 for z >= 3 in float32. gamma, chi2 and beta computed logcdf as
log(cdf) and logsf as log(sf), so the result lost its digits or became 0 when
the probability was close to 1.

gumbel_r.sf now uses -expm1(-exp(-z)). gumbel_l.logcdf now uses log1mexp, which
gumbel_r.logsf already uses. gamma, chi2 and beta use a new helper that
returns log(p) for p < 0.5 and log1p(-q) otherwise, with q = 1 - p taken from
the complementary function (sf or cdf), whose incomplete gamma and beta
evaluations are accurate in that tail. The helper selects the argument of each
branch with jnp.where first, so gradients stay finite.

Test: tests/scipy_stats_test.py passes with and without JAX_ENABLE_X64=1.
testTailsKeepPrecision fails on main for all 8 cases.

head_commit.message:
Fix lax.polynomial derivatives when x broadcasts against coefficients.

When differentiating `lax.polynomial(x, coeffs)` with respect to `x`, the constant coefficient `coeffs[0]` is dropped when computing the derivative polynomial. If `coeffs[0]` had a larger shape than `x` and the remaining coefficients, the resulting tangent was not broadcast to the output shape. Combine tangent terms with `lax.add` and broadcast the output tangent to match the primal output shape and sharding.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42480

head_commit.message:
Plumb the target architecture into layout inference derivation rules.

Derivation rules currently have no way to know which GPU architecture layouts are being inferred for, even though `infer_layout` already receives it. Store the arch on `DerivationContext` and populate it from `infer_layout`. No rule uses it yet.

head_commit.message:
Add `with_logs` option to `jax.grad` and `jax.value_and_grad`.

Collecting backward-pass logs for a scalar-output function previously required
calling `jax.vjp` directly, passing `1.` to `.with_logs`, and unpacking the
cotangent tuple:

```python
# Before:
_, f_vjp = jax.vjp(f, x)
(g,), logs = f_vjp.with_logs(1.)

# After:
g, logs = jax.grad(f, with_logs=True)(x)
```

Both `jax.grad` and `jax.value_and_grad` now accept a keyword-only
`with_logs: bool = False` option:
* `jax.grad(..., with_logs=True)` returns `(g, logs)`, or `(g, aux, logs)` when
  `has_aux=True`.
* `jax.value_and_grad(..., with_logs=True)` pairs `logs` with `g` on the
  backward side, returning `(val, (g, logs))` or `((val, aux), (g, logs))` when
  `has_aux=True`.

display_title: sharding-in-types + reduction_order, plus cleanups

head_commit.message:
sharding-in-types + reduction_order, plus cleanups

Follow-up on cl/1017935155 / #42459.

One cleanup is that we replace some jnp.sum-like helpers (`tiled_sum`, `xlane_sum`, etc) with logic for handling composite reduction orders (like reshapes etc) on high-level `lax.{reduce_sum,reduce_max,dot,dot_general}` (hence `jnp.{sum,max,dot,matmul,einsum}`) and `jax.sharding.reshard` (`is_high=True` when `not is_leaf_order(reduction_order)`, lowered to leaf-only lojax primitives in `to_lojax`), together with helper functions for constructing the corresponding reduction orders like `ro.tiled` and `ro.xlane` where `ro = reduction_order`. As per the description of #42459, lowered lojax primitives still get leaf/primitive reduction orders. We're just moving the logic for handling composite orders into `hijax -> lojax`.

Another cleanup is that we use enums for reduction_order leaves and type parameters.

We also plumb `out_sharding` onto `jnp.sum` and `jnp.max` (and `reduction_order` onto `jax.sharding.reshard`, since it can perform a sum on unreduced arrays, read on to learn more!).

But the main thrust here is making reduction_orders play nicely with sharding-in-types / explicit mode. We raise a `core.ShardingTypeError` if an op's `reduction_order` is not efficiently compatible with the input or result shardings. We also expand the reduction order language to include ring reduction choices (as foretold in #42459's description).

What does 'efficiently compatible' mean? Consider `x: f32[8@X]` with `{X: 2}`:

| Call | Result type | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `jnp.sum(x, reduction_order="unordered")` (or `None`) | `f32[]` | **OK** — binds leaf `reduce_sum`; GSPMD lowers to local reduction + fast tree `all-reduce`. |
| `jnp.sum(x, reduction_order="linear")` | raises `ShardingTypeError` | **Error** — flat `"linear"` across `8@X` would serialize shards; tile local vs cross-shard order explicitly. |
| `jnp.sum(x, out_sharding=P(unreduced={"X"}), reduction_order=ro.tiled(4, "linear", "unreduced"))` | `f32[]{U:X}` | **OK (0 collectives)** — folds each shard's local `f32[4]` with leaf `reduce_sum[linear]` and defers `X` into `{U:X}` (`k_local == 1` at outer level). |
| `jnp.sum(x, reduction_order=ro.tiled(4, "linear", "unordered"))` | `f32[]` | **OK (pinned local + fast all-reduce)** — `reshape(8@X -> (2@X, 4))` -> local `reduce_sum[linear]` -> cross-shard `reduce_sum[unordered]`. |
| `jnp.sum(x2d, axis=0, reduction_order=ro.tiled(4, "linear", ro.ring("bidir", split_axis=0)))` (`x2d: f32[8@X, 16]`) | `f32[16]` | **OK (0-ULP ring all-reduce)** — local `reduce_sum[linear]` -> `(S - 1)`-hop `ppermute` bidirectional ring reduce-scatter splitting output axis 0, followed by `all-gather` to `P(None)`. |
| `jnp.sum(x2d, axis=0, out_sharding=P("X"), reduction_order=ro.tiled(4, "linear", ro.ring("bidir")))` (`x2d: f32[8@X, 16]`) | `f32[16@X]` | **OK (0-ULP ring reduce-scatter)** — local `reduce_sum[linear]` -> `(S - 1)`-hop integer-bitcast `ppermute` bidirectional ring scatter along output axis 0 (`split_axis=0` inferred from `out_sharding=P("X")`). |
| `jax.sharding.reshard(u, P("X"), reduction_order=ro.ring("bidir"))` (`u: f32[16]{U:X}`) | `f32[16@X]` | **OK (0-ULP deferred ring reduce-scatter)** — consumes `{U:X}` partials via the same `(S - 1)`-hop bidirectional ring scatter. |

In words: flat ordered leaves (`"linear"`, `Intrinsic`) cannot reduce across a sharded axis; `"unreduced"` (`ReductionOrder.unreduced`) asserts `k_local == 1` (0 elements reduced at that level) and requires the reduced mesh axis to appear in `out_sharding.spec.unreduced`; and `Ring` lowers sharded ring reductions via `(S - 1)`-hop `shard_map` + integer-bitcast `lax.ppermute` + `optimization_barrier` (followed by `all-gather` when `out_sharding` is replicated along the ring axis) with 0-ULP parity against single-device ring-hop linear accumulation.

In terms of #42459's reference `RedExpr` language and `eval_red(e, X)` (summing along axis 0 of `X` of length `S`):

```python
case Permute(Ring(k, dir), body):  # X has shape (S, ..., D_k, ...)
  S, ax = len(X), (k % (X.ndim - 1)) + 1
  asc = lambda r, c: np.roll(c, -(r + 1), axis=0)
  desc = lambda r, c: np.roll(c, -r, axis=0)[::-1]
  def perm_chunk(r, c):
    if dir in ('asc', 'desc'):
      return asc(r, c) if dir == 'asc' else desc(r, c)
    c0, c1 = np.split(c, 2, axis=ax)
    return np.concatenate([asc(r, c0), desc(r, c1)], axis=ax)
  chunks = [perm_chunk(r, c) for r, c in enumerate(np.split(X, S, axis=ax))]
  return eval_red(body, np.concatenate(chunks, axis=ax))
```

When `out_sharding` shards an output axis `k` on the reduced mesh axis (reduce-scatter), `split_axis` defaults to `k` and the result stays sharded; when `out_sharding` leaves the reduced mesh axis replicated (ring all-reduce), `split_axis` must be given explicitly and an `all-gather` (`reshard`) follows the ring reduce-scatter.

The exact same `R` values generalize to the contracting axis of `jnp.dot` / `jnp.matmul` / `jnp.einsum` (`Tile` reshapes `K` into `(num_tiles, tile)`, runs a shard-local batched `dot_general` with `reduction_order=inner`, and reduces `num_tiles` via `reduce_sum` with `reduction_order=outer`), e.g.:

```python
# Per-shard MXU 256-tiles accumulated linearly in f32, cast to bf16 at shard
# boundary (K_local = 2048), then bidirectional ring reduce-scattered into P(None, "X"):
R_tp = ro.tiled(
    2048,
    inner=ro.cast(jnp.bfloat16, ro.tiled(256, ro.Intrinsic("tpu_v7_mxu_256"), "linear")),
    outer=ro.ring("bidir"),
)
y = jnp.dot(a, b, preferred_element_type=jnp.float32, out_sharding=P(None, "X"), reduction_order=R_tp)
```

### Hijax-to-lojax lowering & autodiff (`AD` before `to_lojax` expansion)

Because composite `Order`s (`Tile`, `Pad`, `Cast`, `Ring`) and `ReductionOrder.unreduced` bind directly on high-level `lax.{reduce_sum_p,reduce_max_p,dot_general_p}` and `pjit.reshard_p`, `jax.make_jaxpr` records a single equation carrying `reduction_order=...` while `pe.lower_jaxpr2` unfolds it to leaf lojax orders only, and autodiff differentiates the hijax equation before `to_lojax`:

1. **`jax.grad` through `ro.ring` (`uint32` wire bitcast + `fori_loop` + `shard_map`):**
   Differentiating `reduce_sum_p` before `to_lojax` transposes directly into a single `broadcast_in_dim` + `reshard` rather than differentiating through `bitcast_convert_type(..., uint32)` (`float0` tangents) and `S - 1` `fori_loop` steps.
2. **`jax.grad` (+ `jax.checkpoint`) through tiled `bf16`-cast `jnp.dot`:**
   Differentiating `dot_general_p` before `to_lojax` keeps `reduction_order` on the forward hijax primal while emitting two untiled full-precision backward `dot_general[reduction_order=None]` calls rather than transposing tiled reshapes or truncating cotangents through `bfloat16`.

| `jax.sharding.reshard(u, P("X"), reduction_order=ro.ring("bidir"))` (`u: f32[16]{U:X}`) | `f32[16@X]` | **OK (0-ULP deferred ring reduce-scatter)** — consumes `{U:X}` partials via the same `(S - 1)`-hop bidirectional ring scatter. |

In words: flat ordered leaves (`"linear"`, `Intrinsic`) cannot reduce across a sharded axis; `"unreduced"` (`ReductionOrder.unreduced`) asserts `k_local == 1` (0 elements reduced at that level) and requires the reduced mesh axis to appear in `out_sharding.spec.unreduced`; and `Ring` lowers sharded ring reductions via `(S - 1)`-hop `shard_map` + integer-bitcast `lax.ppermute` + `optimization_barrier` (followed by `all-gather` when `out_sharding` is replicated along the ring axis) with 0-ULP parity against single-device ring-hop linear accumulation.

In terms of #42459's reference `RedExpr` language and `eval_red(e, X)` (summing along axis 0 of `X` of length `S`):

```python
case Permute(Ring(k, dir), body):  # X has shape (S, ..., D_k, ...)
  S, ax = len(X), (k % (X.ndim - 1)) + 1
  asc = lambda r, c: np.roll(c, -(r + 1), axis=0)
  desc = lambda r, c: np.roll(c, -r, axis=0)[::-1]
  def perm_chunk(r, c):
    if dir in ('asc', 'desc'):
      return asc(r, c) if dir == 'asc' else desc(r, c)
    c0, c1 = np.split(c, 2, axis=ax)
    return np.concatenate([asc(r, c0), desc(r, c1)], axis=ax)
  chunks = [perm_chunk(r, c) for r, c in enumerate(np.split(X, S, axis=ax))]
  return eval_red(body, np.concatenate(chunks, axis=ax))
```

When `out_sharding` shards an output axis `k` on the reduced mesh axis (reduce-scatter), `split_axis` defaults to `k` and the result stays sharded; when `out_sharding` leaves the reduced mesh axis replicated (ring all-reduce), `split_axis` must be given explicitly and an `all-gather` (`reshard`) follows the ring reduce-scatter.

The exact same `R` values generalize to the contracting axis of `jnp.dot` / `jnp.matmul` / `jnp.einsum` (`Tile` reshapes `K` into `(num_tiles, tile)`, runs a shard-local batched `dot_general` with `reduction_order=inner`, and reduces `num_tiles` via `reduce_sum` with `reduction_order=outer`), e.g.:

```python
# Per-shard MXU 256-tiles accumulated linearly in f32, cast to bf16 at shard
# boundary (K_local = 2048), then bidirectional ring reduce-scattered into P(None, "X"):
R_tp = ro.tiled(
    2048,
    inner=ro.cast(jnp.bfloat16, ro.tiled(256, ro.Intrinsic("tpu_v7_mxu_256"), "linear")),
    outer=ro.ring("bidir"),
)
y = jnp.dot(a, b, preferred_element_type=jnp.float32, out_sharding=P(None, "X"), reduction_order=R_tp)
```

### Hijax-to-lojax lowering & autodiff (`AD` before `to_lojax` expansion)

Because composite `Order`s (`Tile`, `Pad`, `Cast`, `Ring`) and `ReductionOrder.unreduced` bind directly on high-level `lax.{reduce_sum_p,reduce_max_p,dot_general_p}` and `pjit.reshard_p`, `jax.make_jaxpr` records a single equation carrying `reduction_order=...` while `pe.lower_jaxpr2` unfolds it to leaf lojax orders only, and autodiff differentiates the hijax equation before `to_lojax`:

1. **`jax.grad` through `ro.ring` (`uint32` wire bitcast + `fori_loop` + `shard_map`):**
   Differentiating `reduce_sum_p` before `to_lojax` transposes directly into a single `broadcast_in_dim` + `reshard` rather than differentiating through `bitcast_convert_type(..., uint32)` (`float0` tangents) and `S - 1` `fori_loop` steps.
2. **`jax.grad` (+ `jax.checkpoint`) through tiled `bf16`-cast `jnp.dot`:**
   Differentiating `dot_general_p` before `to_lojax` keeps `reduction_order` on the forward hijax primal while emitting two untiled full-precision backward `dot_general[reduction_order=None]` calls rather than transposing tiled reshapes or truncating cotangents through `bfloat16`.

Narrow the stats tail fix to the Gumbel functions

Address review of the first revision: evaluating cdf and sf for every element
of gamma, chi2 and beta doubles the work, and the log_with_complement helper
changes NaN handling and gradients at the support boundaries. Those three
distributions are left as on main.

For the closed-form Gumbel functions the cost is nil. gumbel_l.logcdf and
gumbel_r.logsf (log(1 - exp(-exp(z)))) now use a shared helper that switches
to z - exp(z)/2 for z <= -10 (where exp(z) underflowed to -inf in float32 for
z <= -104, with a NaN gradient) and to log1mexp otherwise, with each branch
fed arguments it can handle so gradients stay finite, also where exp(z)
overflows. gumbel_r.sf also masks the overflow of exp(-z) in the gradient.

Test: tests/scipy_stats_test.py passes with and without JAX_ENABLE_X64=1. The
new Gumbel tail and gradient tests fail on main.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] Eliminate redundant XLA compilations in `hyp1f1`, `hyp2f1`, and `betaln` gradient tests

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Eliminate redundant XLA compilations in `hyp1f1`, `hyp2f1`, and `betaln` gradient tests

`hyp1f1` and `hyp2f1` previously applied `promote_args_inexact` inside `@custom_jvp` and `@jit`, wrapped `_hyp1f1_x_derivative` and `_hyp2f1_x_derivative` in an outer `@jit`, and passed the differentiated parameter array `p` directly to `_hyp1f1_param_derivative` / `_hyp2f1_param_derivative`. On mixed-shape or mixed-dtype inputs (such as in `testScipySpecialFun`), this forced `_hyp1f1_x_derivative` and `_hyp2f1_x_derivative` to re-inline and recompile the full `hyp1f1` / `hyp2f1` loop graphs instead of reusing the cached `@jit` executable, and caused `_hyp1f1_param_derivative` / `_hyp2f1_param_derivative` to miss the `@jit` cache across parameters of different broadcast shapes.

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Use `libstdc++` with `linux_glibc_2_35` sysroot under `--config=tsan` in `.bazelrc`

After switching `common:linux` in `.bazelrc` to `--@rules_ml_toolchain//common:stdlib=libc++`, `--@rules_ml_toolchain//common:static_libcxx=True`, `--@llvm-project//llvm:use_libunwind_for_eh_frame_registration=True`, and `--repo_env=SYSROOT_DIST=linux_glibc_2_27`, `--config=tsan` / `--config=tsan_shared` links `rules_ml_toolchain`'s prebuilt static `libc++.a`, which is not compiled with ThreadSanitizer instrumentation. Uninstrumented out-of-line synchronization in `libc++.a` (such as `std::__call_once` and `std::__shared_weak_count::__release_shared`) prevents TSan from observing release-acquire happens-before edges across threads and also mixes static `libc++` / `libunwind` with the `libstdc++`-built TSAN NumPy wheel in `.github/workflows/tsan.yaml`.

Override `common:tsan` in `.bazelrc` to use `stdlib=libstdc++`, `static_libcxx=False`, `use_libunwind_for_eh_frame_registration=False`, and `SYSROOT_DIST=linux_glibc_2_35` (matching `common:oneapi` for C++20 `libstdc++` support on the Ubuntu 22.04 `ml-build` container).
